title: Bringing back Joe Capraro and Charlie Cadello
summary: Mares brought Capraro and Cadello back to record after twenty years of retirement.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, there's two or three other boys here. For instance, we take like Joe Capera. Back in the early 30s, Joe was one of the big names around New Orleans. In fact, he was the only one who had a band around here. Joe faded out. I brought Joe back also after 20 years' retirement. In my book, Joe's one of the greatest guitar boys in the business. He's a good rhythm boy. He knows what it's all about. Another fellow here I'd like to bring on is Charlie Cadela. Charlie and my brother Paul were very, very good friends. I've always been good friends with Charlie all my life. I always enjoyed his playing. I thought Charlie was one of the greats that belong up there with Sidney Arrigan and Raymond Boyk and rap and Fars and those kind of fellas. And I did want to have Charlie on my label. Well, Charlie had been retired for about 20 years also. So I said, look, man, start fooling with that clarinet in about a month from now, I'm going to come back at you. I don't want no finance. I'm telling you to start playing a little bit. Well, about a month I came back. He said, well, I believe I can make four tunes. I said, well, here, I got four tunes picked. How do they sound to you? Well, he said, three of them's all right. Give me nobody, sweetheart, because I like that tune and I know it. I said, well, it's yours. So we made the session and that came out very good. And you still can hear Charlie with that beautiful harmonizing clarinet that was so popular in the early days. Sounded a lot like the rap's tone sometimes. You can hardly tell them apart.
